title: From Crisis to Prosperity: AI and Open Finance for Holistic Financial Health and Smart Future Planning
authors: Bukovski, Kal; Jain, Kushagra; Cummins, Mark; Bowden, James; Tetteh, Godsway Korku; Lin, Zi
venue: Financial Regulation Innovation Lab White Paper
tldr: This whitepaper proposes an AI-driven framework for holistic financial health evaluation using Open Finance data, presenting a Smart Personalised Finance Management system with persona-based guidance and sequential optimisation.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional credit-score-centric frameworks fail to capture the full spectrum of consumers' financial health. The COVID-19 pandemic and cost-of-living crises exposed vulnerabilities in reactive, one-dimensional risk models. Consumers and institutions require proactive, resilience-focused insights spanning day-to-day cashflow management, medium-term debt servicing, and long-term wealth accumulation. Only 8% of UK adults currently receive financial advice, creating a significant 'advice gap'.
approach: Proposed a comprehensive framework integrating Open Finance data with AI and ML techniques.
Developed a Smart Personalised Finance Management Framework with hierarchical financial needs.
Applied clustering techniques (K-means, DBSCAN, hierarchical) for customer segmentation.
Implemented sequential optimisation engine with three layers of financial guidance.
Incorporated explainable AI techniques (SHAP, LIME) for transparency and regulatory compliance.
Used Monte Carlo simulations and Geometric Brownian Motion for stochastic modelling.
Mapped persona archetypes to tailored optimisation plans aligned with FCA's Advice Guidance Boundary Review.
findings: Open Finance extends beyond Open Banking to encompass mortgages, savings, pensions, investments, insurance, and government benefits.
Financial health consists of four pillars: Spend, Save, Borrow, and Plan, with resilience as a cross-cutting capability.

Eight distinct customer personas identified through clustering: Emerging Professionals with Debt, Disciplined Debt Navigators, Established and Secure Homeowners, Vulnerable and Delinquent Renters, Affluent and Prudent Investors, Struggling to Start, Steady and Responsible Managers, Crisis-Prone and Underbanked.
Hierarchical financial needs framework prioritises cash flow stability before debt management, then wealth accumulation, then legacy planning.
Privacy-preserving techniques including GANs and VAEs enable synthetic data generation while maintaining statistical properties.
Behavioural interventions like soft goal setting causally increases savings rate, especially for low-income individuals.
ML models trained on Open Finance data can identify early warning indicators of financial distress.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This whitepaper contributes to FinTech and personal finance literature by proposing a comprehensive framework for holistic financial health evaluation using Open Finance data and AI. It introduces a hierarchical financial needs framework inspired by Maslow's theory, mapping it to a sequential optimisation engine with three layers of guidance. The identification of 8 distinct customer personas through clustering provides actionable insights for personalized financial services. The paper also addresses critical regulatory alignment with FCA's Advice Guidance Boundary Review and Consumer Duty framework, demonstrating how AI-driven guidance can bridge the advice gap while maintaining ethical standards.

limits: White paper format rather than peer-reviewed research study.
UK-centric focus may limit generalizability to other financial systems.
No empirical validation of proposed framework presented.
Focus on developed economy context may not apply to emerging markets.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan of all 14 topic domains revealed primary relevance to Domains 4, 5, 10, and 12. Topic 4.A (Predictive Modeling) received high relevance as the paper proposes ML-based cash flow modelling for financial health. Topic 5.A (Financial Behavioral Profiles) received medium relevance for behavioural finance principles. Topic 5.B (Customer Segmentation) received high relevance for the 8 persona clusters identified. Topic 10.A (Algorithmic Trust) received medium relevance for ethical AI discussion. Topic 10.B (AI-Driven Advising) received high relevance for the core framework proposal. Topic 12.B (Evaluation) received medium relevance for model performance evaluation. Domains 1-3, 6-9, 11, 13-14 were considered and rejected as the paper does not address Filipino demographics, expense categorization algorithms, anomaly detection, mobile design, data privacy mechanisms (beyond mentioning), savings/debt management specifics, or synthetic data generation techniques.
